record.paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
record.context_brief: Whether to abandon ADM and other parametrizations
record.original_question: Should the ADM Hamiltonian formulation, or other Hamiltonian formulations based on parametrizations whose canonicity is unproved in the usual phase space, be abandoned or treated as independent models rather than as valid formulations of Einstein General Relativity?

evidence.quote: Should we abandon the ADM formulation because the new ADM variables are not related with the old ones by a canonical transformation? Should we also abandon any other parametrizations if they do not satisfy this criterion?
Then, should we consider the ADM formulation as a model named, say, “ADM gravity”, without any reference to Einstein General Relativity, as Kiriushcheva and Kuzmin suggest?
However, the results are rather indicative, so I cannot see any reason to abandon the ADM parametrization or other possible parametrizations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Einstein's General Relativity, whose Lagrangian is the Einstein–Hilbert action on a globally hyperbolic spacetime. The standard Arnowitt–Deser–Misner (ADM) Hamiltonian formulation arises by performing a 3+1 decomposition of the spacetime metric g_{\mu
u} into the lapse N, shift N^i, and spatial 3-metric h_{ij}, taken as new configuration variables in place of the components of g_{\mu
u}. A Hamiltonian formulation is said to be canonically equivalent to another if the change of variables on phase space (together with the corresponding redefinition of momenta) is a canonical transformation in the standard sense — i.e. preserves the symplectic form / Poisson brackets — on the full phase space without restriction to constraint surfaces.

It is known that the change of variables from (g_{\mu
u}, \pi^{\mu
u}) to the ADM variables (N, N^i, h_{ij}) and their conjugate momenta has not been shown to be a canonical transformation on the full unconstrained phase space; analogous statements hold for various other 3+1 parametrizations (e.g. tetrad/triad-based, or those using different combinations of metric components).

Question. Determine whether the following position is mathematically justified: any Hamiltonian formulation of gravity built from a parametrization of the spacetime metric whose relation to the original metric variables is not implemented by a canonical transformation on the usual phase space should be regarded as an independent dynamical model (not equivalent to the Hamiltonian formulation of Einstein's General Relativity), rather than as a legitimate Hamiltonian reformulation of Einstein's theory. Equivalently, decide whether the ADM formulation and similar parametrization-based Hamiltonian formulations must be abandoned as formulations of Einstein General Relativity, or whether they remain physically and mathematically equivalent to it despite the absence of a proven canonical transformation between the variables.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a methodological/foundational one in the canonical formulation of general relativity. The literature (Kiriushcheva–Kuzmin and responses) shows the issue is debated rather than settled by a definitive theorem; no widely accepted resolution proving that ADM must be abandoned, nor a complete proof of canonical equivalence on the full phase space, has been established. Status remains unclear.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian formulation of GR (Kiriushcheva–Kuzmin debate)
status_evidence.snippet: Kiriushcheva and Kuzmin argue ADM variables are not related to metric variables by a canonical transformation, raising doubts about ADM equivalence to Einstein GR.
status_evidence.claim: The canonical equivalence of ADM and the metric Hamiltonian formulation is contested in the literature.
